motion.name: line-interval
motion.purpose: One ledger line prints every 520ms while the ledger is visible and the tab is shown.

motion.name: print-line
motion.purpose: The newest line wipes in left to right, in print-head steps.

motion.name: carriage
motion.purpose: A paper-colored carriage block crosses the print head, then lifts away.

motion.name: stamp-down
motion.purpose: A BIG TRADE stamp lands from 1.35x, overshoots to 0.96x, settles at its -4deg tilt.

motion.name: ticket-out
motion.purpose: The queue ticket feeds down out of the machine; not replayed when restored from storage.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Ledger stays on its server-rendered still frame (line 96); no print, carriage or stamp-down. ticket-out should also stop (not yet gated in the build).

narrative.overview:
The public site is an Indonesian bank passbook lying open on its cobalt cloth cover. Every trade is a dot-matrix line in ribbon ink with the broker who bought and the broker who sold; the bank's own pre-printed form sits underneath in cobalt; the teller's violet rubber stamp marks what matters. Nothing glows and nothing floats: depth is paper on cloth, ink on paper, and a ticket torn from a queue machine.

Two type voices carry the whole system. Archivo, pushed wide for headings and narrow for form labels, is the bank's printed stationery. Doto is the printer: one size for every ledger line, with rank made by striking harder, reversing, or stamping, never by printing bigger. Color is scarce and assigned by material: cobalt is cloth and form ink, violet is stamp ink, green and red are reserved for prices.

The page is calm where the passbook is calm (wide paper, generous sheet padding) and live where the market is live: one line prints every 520 ms under a moving print head, and the newest line is always the darkest.
keyCharacteristics: Cobalt cloth ground with a woven thread texture; pale green security paper sheets with a tiling guilloche.
Two faces: Archivo Variable (width axis) for the form, Doto Variable for every printed entry.
One ledger print size; rank by double-strike, reversal, underline and stamps.
Cobalt form ink for pre-printed headers and column rules, ribbon ink for entries.
Violet rubber stamps with uneven inking; green and red only on prices.
Motion is the printer's: line print, carriage, stamp-down, ticket-out. All of it is decoration on a readable still frame.

rules.name: The Prices-Only Rule
rules.body: Green and red appear on prices and nowhere else, except red for a form error. Broker codes, lots, values and nets stay in ribbon ink; direction is read from the sign.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Anything pre-printed by the bank (column headers, column rules, table-head rules) is cobalt form ink; anything the machine printed is ribbon ink. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Ribbon Fade Rule
rules.body: In a running ledger the newest line is darkest; each older line mixes ink toward the paper by 3% per line, capped at 32% so every line stays above 4.5:1. Prices keep their full side ink.

rules.name: The One Print Size Rule
rules.body: Inside a ledger every printed line is 15px (13px under 420px). Rank comes from double-strike (900 weight plus a 0.6px shadow strike), reversal (ink ground, paper text), a heavier rule, or a stamp, never from a larger size.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy in Archivo is set by weight and width together: wide and heavy for headings, narrow and tracked for labels. Don't add a second sans.

rules.name: The Paper-Thickness Rule
rules.body: The hard 1 to 2px line under a sheet is paper thickness, and the button's 2px lip is key travel that disappears on press. Neither is a decorative offset shadow; don't add hard offsets anywhere else.

dos: Do set every ledger entry in Doto at the one print size (15px, 13px under 420px) and rank lines with double-strike, reversal, rules or a stamp.
Do put pre-printed form parts (headers, column rules) in cobalt and machine-printed entries in ribbon ink.
Do fade older ledger lines toward the paper by at most 32% and keep the newest darkest.
Do reserve green and red for prices, with red also allowed for a form error.
Do lay content on security paper sheets over the cobalt cloth, with the sheet shadow and paper-edge line.
Do keep motion to the printer's grammar (line print, carriage, stamp-down, ticket-out) and render a complete still frame with all of it off under reduced motion.
donts: Don't print a ledger line larger to make it important; double-strike or stamp it.
Don't use violet for anything but stamps, focus, caret and selection.
Don't add glows, gradients on type, or a dark screenshot hero; the passbook is paper and ink.
Don't box the email field; it is a dashed line on the form.
Don't add hard offset shadows beyond paper thickness and the button's key lip.
Don't stamp calls to action; a stamp records a fact about a trade or the record.
